question.text: How do changes in automotive radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Vector Network Analyzer?

exchange.sent: How do changes in automotive radar technology affect the measurement capability required from Vector Network Analyzer?

answer.answer:
The passages do not directly state a causal rule, but they support this inference: as automotive radar moves to wider instantaneous bandwidths and higher mmWave bands, the VNA must cover wider frequency spans, support time-domain analysis, and provide sufficient bandwidth/dynamic range for flatness, group delay, and ghost-object measurements [24][4][5][30].
| Automotive radar technology change | Measurement capability required from VNA | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AREG800A IF bandwidth options expand from 1 GHz to 2 GHz or 5 GHz, with IF frequency ranges listed as 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz | VNA measurements must cover the corresponding wider IF spans; AREG800A VNA conditions list spans of 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [24][5] | [24][5] |
| Ghost-object suppression is measured with a vector network analyzer in time domain | The VNA needs time-domain measurement capability, with frequency step size 125 kHz, measurement bandwidth 100 kHz, source power –10 dBm, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [4] | [4] |
| 76 GHz to 81 GHz automotive radar frontends and QAT100 use RF frequency ranges in the 76 GHz to 81 GHz band, and QAT100 has 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth | VNA or VNA system capability must reach mmWave automotive radar bands when measuring RF paths; the ZNA67EXT VNA system covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz, while the base ZNA series covers up to 67 GHz [24][31][18][12] | [24][31][18][12] |
| Automotive radar echo generation supports dynamic artificial objects, distances up to 3000 m, and Doppler / velocity functions | VNA-related measurements in the passages focus on transfer characteristics and ghost-object suppression, while Doppler frequency offset accuracy is measured with a spectrum analyzer, not a VNA [29][27][4][5] | [29][27][4][5] |
【推論】Therefore, wider-band automotive radar technology increases the needed VNA frequency-span and bandwidth-related measurement coverage from about 1 GHz IF spans toward 5 GHz IF spans, because AREG800A bandwidth options and VNA measurement spans scale from 1.1–2.1 GHz to 0.7–5.7 GHz [24][5].  
【推論】For 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar frontend work, a base VNA limited to 67 GHz would not by itself cover the full 76–81 GHz RF band, while the ZNA67EXT system’s 10 MHz to 110 GHz range covers that band [24][12][18].

- [[Hybrid eCall testing]] 以 EN 18052:2025 與 hybrid fallback 為核心；本頁聚焦 EN 17240:2024 NG eCall verification，不描述 classic CS fallback 或 EN 18052 test scope。
- [[cetecom advanced certifies Rohde & Schwarz test solution for hybrid and Next Generation eCall testing]] 提到 EN 17240:2024+A1:2026 與 cetecom advanced certification testing；本頁來源只提 EN 17240:2024，且未說第三方 certification report。

- [[WLAN]] signaling 與 WLAN TX measurements，涵蓋 802.11a/b/g/n/ac、802.11ax、802.11be、802.11bn 與 2x2 MIMO。
- [[Fading]]、[[AWGN]]、[[BLER]]、[[CSI report]]、[[Throughput measurement]]、[[PER measurement]]。

- 標準：[[EN 17240]]:2024。
- 測試情境：simulating a [[PSAP]]。
- 驗證內容：NG eCall including voice and data transmission，並 validated the compliance of the implementation at both ends with EN 17240:2024。

The passages do not directly state a causal rule, but they support this inference: as automotive radar moves to wider instantaneous bandwidths and higher mmWave bands, the VNA must cover wider frequency spans, support time-domain analysis, and provide sufficient bandwidth/dynamic range for flatness, group delay, and ghost-object measurements [24][4][5][30].
| Automotive radar technology change | Measurement capability required from VNA | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AREG800A IF bandwidth options expand from 1 GHz to 2 GHz or 5 GHz, with IF frequency ranges listed as 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz | VNA measurements must cover the corresponding wider IF spans; AREG800A VNA conditions list spans of 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [24][5] | [24][5] |
| Ghost-object suppression is measured with a vector network analyzer in time domain | The VNA needs time-domain measurement capability, with frequency step size 125 kHz, measurement bandwidth 100 kHz, source power –10 dBm, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [4] | [4] |
| 76 GHz to 81 GHz automotive radar frontends and QAT100 use RF frequency ranges in the 76 GHz to 81 GHz band, and QAT100 has 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth | VNA or VNA system capability must reach mmWave automotive radar bands when measuring RF paths; the ZNA67EXT VNA system covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz, while the base ZNA series covers up to 67 GHz [24][31][18][12] | [24][31][18][12] |
| Automotive radar echo generation supports dynamic artificial objects, distances up to 3000 m, and Doppler / velocity functions | VNA-related measurements in the passages focus on transfer characteristics and ghost-object suppression, while Doppler frequency offset accuracy is measured with a spectrum analyzer, not a VNA [29][27][4][5] | [29][27][4][5] |
【推論】Therefore, wider-band automotive radar technology increases the needed VNA frequency-span and bandwidth-related measurement coverage from about 1 GHz IF spans toward 5 GHz IF spans, because AREG800A bandwidth options and VNA measurement spans scale from 1.1–2.1 GHz to 0.7–5.7 GHz [24][5].  
【推論】For 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar frontend work, a base VNA limited to 67 GHz would not by itself cover the full 76–81 GHz RF band, while the ZNA67EXT system’s 10 MHz to 110 GHz range covers that band [24][12][18].

The passages do not directly state a causal rule, but they support this inference: as automotive radar moves to wider instantaneous bandwidths and higher mmWave bands, the VNA must cover wider frequency spans, support time-domain analysis, and provide sufficient bandwidth/dynamic range for flatness, group delay, and ghost-object measurements [24][4][5][30].
| Automotive radar technology change | Measurement capability required from VNA | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AREG800A IF bandwidth options expand from 1 GHz to 2 GHz or 5 GHz, with IF frequency ranges listed as 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz | VNA measurements must cover the corresponding wider IF spans; AREG800A VNA conditions list spans of 1.1 GHz to 2.1 GHz, 0.7 GHz to 2.7 GHz, and 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz [24][5] | [24][5] |
| Ghost-object suppression is measured with a vector network analyzer in time domain | The VNA needs time-domain measurement capability, with frequency step size 125 kHz, measurement bandwidth 100 kHz, source power –10 dBm, and spans up to 0.7 GHz to 5.7 GHz depending on bandwidth [4] | [4] |
| 76 GHz to 81 GHz automotive radar frontends and QAT100 use RF frequency ranges in the 76 GHz to 81 GHz band, and QAT100 has 4 GHz RF instantaneous bandwidth | VNA or VNA system capability must reach mmWave automotive radar bands when measuring RF paths; the ZNA67EXT VNA system covers 10 MHz to 110 GHz, while the base ZNA series covers up to 67 GHz [24][31][18][12] | [24][31][18][12] |
| Automotive radar echo generation supports dynamic artificial objects, distances up to 3000 m, and Doppler / velocity functions | VNA-related measurements in the passages focus on transfer characteristics and ghost-object suppression, while Doppler frequency offset accuracy is measured with a spectrum analyzer, not a VNA [29][27][4][5] | [29][27][4][5] |
【推論】Therefore, wider-band automotive radar technology increases the needed VNA frequency-span and bandwidth-related measurement coverage from about 1 GHz IF spans toward 5 GHz IF spans, because AREG800A bandwidth options and VNA measurement spans scale from 1.1–2.1 GHz to 0.7–5.7 GHz [24][5].  
【推論】For 76 GHz to 81 GHz radar frontend work, a base VNA limited to 67 GHz would not by itself cover the full 76–81 GHz RF band, while the ZNA67EXT system’s 10 MHz to 110 GHz range covers that band [24][12][18].
